output.summary: An aquatic perennial native from East Asia through northern Indochina to central and northern India, with isolated Caspian locations. Its flowers can regulate their temperature, and seeds have germinated after about 1,300 years. Rhizomes and seeds are widely eaten; petals, leaves and rhizomes should be cooked because eating them raw risks parasite transmission.
output.edibilityNote: All parts are edible; petals, leaves and rhizomes are recommended cooked because raw consumption risks parasite transmission.
